# Zoomies

_Take and copy paste screen in 2 seconds. Rename? 3 seconds. Rename + annotate with prompt for agent? 5 seconds. Quick edit? 7? maybe 10..._

> **Requires macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later.** If you have an older macOS version, it is probably best to use this as a product spec and build your own. I had enough headaches with older OS versions already.
>
> Zoomies builds natively on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Intel is supported but untested because I do not have an Intel Mac.

Mac-only keyboard-first screenshot and scratchpad app for agentic coding.
Good for touchpad users too, especially if your wrist is already cooked from gaming.

Fork it, pork it, change it, rebuild it. Have fun.

## What It Does

- Captures the exact UI state you want a coding agent to understand.
- Adds quick notes/prompts to screenshots so the context travels with the image.
- Saves Zoomies edit data inside PNGs, so future reopens can edit/delete Zoomies-added arrows, text, pen strokes, shapes, pasted selections, and cut regions.
- Creates quick scratchpad notes for errors, issues, and ideas you spot in one project while your head is still in another.
- Lets you rename, annotate, save, copy, or delete without breaking coding flow.
- Reopens a selected Finder image and sends it back through the Zoomies flow.

When you edit and save a non-PNG image such as a JPEG or HEIC, Zoomies saves the
edited result as a PNG and removes the original non-PNG file.

## Quick Start

```bash
cd zoomies
swift build
swift run Zoomies
```

To build a clickable `.app`:

```bash
./scripts/build_app.sh
open dist/Zoomies.app
```

A coding agent can run that build script for you too.

### Building on an Intel Mac

Intel users should build Zoomies from source on their Intel Mac:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/bald-ai/zoomies.git
cd zoomies
./scripts/build_app.sh
open dist/Zoomies.app
```

Swift automatically builds for the Mac it is running on: Apple silicon produces
an `arm64` app, while Intel produces an `x86_64` app. A universal binary is only
needed when distributing one prebuilt `.app` for both architectures; this
repository distributes source instead.

Intel support requires an Intel Mac running macOS 14 or later with Xcode 15 or
later. **I do not own an Intel Mac, so the Intel build has not been personally
tested.**

## Default Shortcuts

- `Option+Shift+4` -> area capture
- `Option+Shift+3` -> full-screen capture
- `Option+Shift+2` -> select an image in Finder, press this to edit/rename it with Zoomies
- `Option+Shift+1` -> create a scratchpad note
- `Option+Shift+5` -> start/stop screen recording (requires macOS 15)

The defaults intentionally avoid the standard macOS `Cmd+Shift` screenshot shortcuts.

You can change the main global shortcuts in Zoomies Settings. If you want to
change keybinds that are not exposed in the UI, ask your coding agent to update
the relevant shortcut code and build a new `.app` for you.

## Workflow Keybinds

| Screen | Key | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rename / Prompt | `Enter` | Save |
| Rename / Prompt | `Cmd+Enter` | Copy + save |
| Rename / Prompt | `Cmd+Backspace` | Copy + delete |
| Rename / Prompt | `Esc` | Delete / close |
| Flow | `Tab` | Next step |
| Flow | `Shift+Tab` | Previous step |
| Edit | `W` / `A` / `R` / `E` / `T` / `S` | Pen / arrow / rectangle / ellipse / text / select |
| Edit | `K` or `Q` | Open colors |
| Edit | `1-6` | Pick color |
| Edit | `Cmd+Z` / `Cmd+Shift+Z` | Undo / redo |
| Edit | `Option+Backspace` | Clear |
| Edit | `Cmd+C` / `Cmd+X` / `Cmd+V` | Copy / cut / paste |
| Edit | `Cmd +` / `Cmd -` / `Cmd 0` | Zoom in / out / reset |
| Edit | `Enter` | Save |
| Edit | `Cmd+Enter` | Copy + save |
| Edit | `Esc` | Cancel |

## Editor Select Tool

Press `S` in the editor to use Select.

Select now has two jobs:

- Click a Zoomies-added object, like text, arrow, pen stroke, rectangle, ellipse, pasted image, or cut/erase region, to select it.
- Drag the selected object to move it, or press `Delete` to remove it.
- Drag on empty screenshot space to select a rectangular image region.
- With a region selected, use `Cmd+C` to copy it, `Cmd+X` to cut it, and `Cmd+V` to paste it back into the canvas.
- Switching to another tool clears the rectangular area selection.

Select does not change the contents or shape of an existing annotation. To edit
existing text, press `T` for the Text tool and double-click the text. Arrows,
pen strokes, rectangles, and ellipses can be moved or deleted, but not reshaped.

Editable objects are remembered only for PNGs saved by this version of Zoomies or later. Older already-flattened screenshots still open as normal images because their arrows/text are already baked into the pixels.

## Screen Recording

`Option+Shift+5` or the menu-bar icon's Start Recording begins a display
recording. There is no display picker: recording starts on the display under
the pointer and follows the pointer to another monitor after it stays there
for half a second. It keeps recording across app and Space changes, includes
the cursor, excludes Zoomies' own windows, and stops automatically after 60
seconds.

Video is 30, 60, or 120 fps (selectable in Settings, default 30), SDR, H.264 MP4 without audio on a fixed 1920x1080 canvas
(the full display is fitted without cropping or stretching, with black
margins where needed). The menu bar shows only the elapsed seconds, from `0` to `60`, in red. The finished video is saved beside screenshots with a unique
`Recording_...` filename and revealed in Finder.

Only one Zoomies operation runs at a time: recording blocks
screenshots/notes/Finder-reopen, and those workflows block recording startup.
Screen recording requires macOS 15 or later; on macOS 14 the menu command
explains it is unavailable while screenshots and notes keep working.

## Temporary Clipboard Files

`Copy + Delete` needs a temporary file so macOS can still paste the screenshot
after Zoomies removes it from the Desktop. Zoomies stores that temporary copy in
`~/Library/Caches/zoomies/clipboard` and clears the folder the next time Zoomies
starts.

## Permissions

Area capture uses the built-in macOS screenshot selector. Full-screen capture uses `ScreenCaptureKit` (`SCScreenshotManager`). macOS will prompt for Screen Recording permission when needed.

For area capture, drag to select, press Space to switch to window/menu selection, or press Escape to cancel. The captured image then opens in the usual Zoomies workflow.

- **Screen Recording** (for screenshots via ScreenCaptureKit)
- **Automation / Finder** (for reopening flow on selected Finder image via `Option+Shift+2`)

### Permission after rebuilding the app

If you edit the code and build a new copy of Zoomies, macOS may ask for
permission again even though Zoomies still appears to be allowed in System
Settings. The listed permission can belong to the previous app build.

Open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, select the relevant permission,
use the **−** button to remove the old Zoomies entry, then use the **+** button
to add and allow the newly built `Zoomies.app`.

## Permissions

Area capture uses the built-in macOS screenshot selector. Full-screen capture uses `ScreenCaptureKit` (`SCScreenshotManager`). macOS will prompt for Screen Recording permission when needed.

For area capture, drag to select, press Space to switch to window/menu selection, or press Escape to cancel. The captured image then opens in the usual Zoomies workflow.

- **Screen Recording** (for screenshots via ScreenCaptureKit)
- **Automation / Finder** (for reopening flow on selected Finder image via `Option+Shift+2`)

### Permission after rebuilding the app

If you edit the code and build a new copy of Zoomies, macOS may ask for
permission again even though Zoomies still appears to be allowed in System
Settings. The listed permission can belong to the previous app build.

Open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, select the relevant permission,
use the **−** button to remove the old Zoomies entry, then use the **+** button
to add and allow the newly built `Zoomies.app`.

Summary:
<summary>
## 1. Request and Intent

### Enduring objective

Implement numbered annotation markers in the Zoomies macOS screenshot editor according to:

`/Users/applelevne/Documents/coding-projects/zoomies/work/cursor-agents/numbered-markers/spec.md`

The original specification’s intended end state is:

- `F` selects a numbered marker tool rather than `N`.
- Toolbar tooltip is exactly `Numbered marker (F)`.
- Clicking places sequential markers `1`, `2`, `3`, etc. in the current annotation color.
- Markers are filled, have contrasting numerals and outlines, remain readable on light/dark backgrounds, scale exactly like existing text sizing, and support multiple digits without clipping.
- Markers are first-class editable objects supporting selection, movement, deletion, undo/redo, clear, rendering/export, and embedded PNG metadata round trips.
- Existing PNGs without marker metadata remain compatible.
- Deleting markers does not renumber remaining markers; normal sequential placement avoids duplicates and continues beyond the maximum number on reopen.
- Double-clicking a marker allows editing its positive integer number using the existing inline text interaction.
- No separate prompt UI is added; existing note/footer behavior remains the mechanism for note references.
- README shortcut/tool documentation and meaningful tests must be updated.
- `swift test` must pass.
- The user explicitly prohibited building/installing/relaunching the app.

### Current subtask

After the initial implementation passed all 246 tests, an independent review identified four concrete defects. The current request is to fix them in the same checkout while preserving all existing work:

1. `setTool` must end inline editing when switching between Text and Marker, while preserving same-tool editing behavior. Add regression tests in both directions.
2. Cursor preview must be invalidated after undo/redo/clear/deleting the highest marker. Add a testable invalidation hook/window spy if practical.
3. Palette color changes currently directly assign `canvasView.currentColor`; all color updates must refresh marker preview. Prefer `currentColor`’s `didSet` and remove redundant invalidation paths. Verify palette shortcut behavior.
4. Prevent `Int.max` overflow in `nextMarkerNumber`. Define a supported maximum, consistently validate inline/restored values, make next-number calculation overflow-safe, and gracefully refuse placement when the range is exhausted. Add edge/restored-value regression tests.

The user also clarified that marker diameter should continue to use the same scaling calculation as text font size; the numeral itself being rendered at half the diameter is acceptable because the requirement is about shared scaling behavior.

## 2. Key Concepts and Values

### Repository and paths

- Repository/workspace: `/Users/applelevne/Documents/coding-projects/zoomies`
- Specification: `/Users/applelevne/Documents/coding-projects/zoomies/work/cursor-agents/numbered-markers/spec.md`
- Sources scope: `/Users/applelevne/Documents/coding-projects/zoomies/Sources`
- Tests scope: `/Users/applelevne/Documents/coding-projects/zoomies/Tests`
- README scope: `/Users/applelevne/Documents/coding-projects/zoomies/README.md`
- Current branch: `main`
- No branches, commits, worktrees, or delegation are allowed.

### Relevant architecture

- `EditorCanvasState.swift`
  - Codable persisted editor state.
  - Existing item cases include pen, arrow, rectangle, ellipse, text, image, and erase.
  - Marker support was added as `Item.marker(Marker)`.
- `EditorImageRenderer.swift`
  - Runtime `EditorDrawing.Item` model.
  - Shared annotation rendering, bounds calculation, shifting, composite/export behavior, and state conversion.
- `EditorCanvasView.swift`
  - Tool selection, mouse handling, text editing, selection/movement/delete, undo/redo, cursor behavior, and canvas state.
- `EditorWindowController.swift`
  - Toolbar construction, color palette, palette keyboard shortcuts, and canvas setup.
- `PNGMetadata.swift`
  - Embeds/extracts editable `EditorCanvasState` in PNG `iTXt` metadata.
- `README.md`
  - Editor shortcut/tool documentation.
- Tests are in `Tests/ZoomiesTests`.

### Important existing values and design decisions

- Existing text-size calculation:
  - `defaultTextFontSize = round(38.4 / max(0.01, textCreationZoomFactor))`
- Marker diameter intentionally reuses `defaultTextFontSize`.
- Supported marker maximum introduced in the current subtask:
  - `EditorDrawing.MarkerItem.maxNumber = 999_999`
- Marker numbering normally derives from current items as `max(existing marker numbers) + 1`.
- For a state with no markers, next number is `1`.
- If the maximum supported number is already present, next number becomes `nil`; placement should be refused rather than wrapping.
- Marker geometry is a rounded capsule:
  - Single-digit/small values produce a circle-like shape.
  - Wider values expand horizontally based on measured numeral width.
- Contrast uses `NSColor.isLight`:
  - Light fill → black numeral/outline.
  - Dark fill → white numeral/outline.
- Existing cursor infrastructure uses `resetCursorRects`, `addCursorRect`, and `NSCursor(image:hotSpot:)`.
- Existing tests before the review fixes: 246 total, all passing.

## 3. Task Requirements

### Scope and process

The user explicitly requires:

- Preserve all existing edits.
- Work in the existing checkout and branch only.
- Do not delegate further.
- Do not create branches or worktrees.
- Do not commit.
- Only edit declared write scopes: `README.md`, `Sources`, and `Tests`.
- Do not build/install/relaunch the user’s app.
- Read the specification first.
- Run targeted tests and full `swift test`.
- Report exact checks and any remaining limitations.

### Marker implementation requirements

The implementation must provide:

- `F` keyboard shortcut for marker tool.
- Toolbar marker button with tooltip `Numbered marker (F)`.
- Sequential placement in current annotation color.
- Filled marker with contrasting numeral and outline.
- Marker dimensions tied to existing text sizing calculation, including zoom/export behavior.
- Multiple digits without clipping.
- Selection and movement.
- Delete.
- Undo/redo.
- Clear.
- Renderer/export support.
- Embedded PNG metadata round trip.
- Compatibility with old PNGs that do not contain marker state.
- Continue beyond existing maximum after reopening.
- Avoid duplicate numbers during normal sequential placement.
- Preserve numbering behavior through tool switches, undo, redo, and deletion.
- Double-click inline positive integer editing.
- Clean cancel behavior.
- No new prompt UI.

### Review-fix requirements

#### Tool switching and inline editing

`EditorCanvasView.setTool(_:)` must:

- End/commit inline editing when the target tool differs from the tool that owns the editor.
- Specifically fix Text → Marker and Marker → Text.
- Preserve usual same-tool behavior: reselecting the same tool must not tear down the edit.
- Add regression tests for both directions.

Current implementation added:

```swift
if textEditor != nil {
    let editingTool: EditorTool = editingMarkerIndex != nil ? .marker : .text
    if tool != editingTool {
        endTextEditingIfNeeded()
    }
}
```

#### Cursor invalidation

The marker cursor preview must refresh when the next marker number can change, including:

- Placement.
- Undo.
- Redo.
- Clear.
- Deletion, especially deleting the highest-numbered marker.
- Tool changes.
- Color changes.
- Zoom-factor changes.

A test/debug hook was added:

```swift
var onMarkerCursorInvalidation: (() -> Void)?
```

`invalidateMarkerCursorPreview()` should invoke this hook in addition to invalidating cursor rects. Tests should use it if practical.

#### Color updates

The palette controller directly assigns `canvasView.currentColor`, so all assignments must trigger cursor invalidation. Current implementation changed the property to:

```swift
var currentColor: NSColor = .systemRed {
    didSet { invalidateMarkerCursorPreview() }
}
```

`setColor(_:)` now only assigns `currentColor` to avoid redundant invalidation. Palette shortcut paths should be verified.

#### Marker maximum and overflow

A supported maximum marker number must be enforced consistently:

- Persisted/restored marker validation must reject values above the maximum.
- Inline edits must reject values above the maximum.
- Normal placement must not overflow.
- If all supported numbers are exhausted, placement must fail gracefully.
- Do not silently wrap or crash.
- Add tests for maximum values, restored states, and exhausted range.
- Current chosen maximum: `999_999`.

Current state safety change:

```swift
case .marker(let marker):
    return marker.number >= 1
        && marker.number <= EditorDrawing.MarkerItem.maxNumber
        ...
```

Current overflow-safe next-number logic:

```swift
private var nextMarkerNumber: Int? {
    guard let maxNumber = items.lazy.compactMap({ item -> Int? in
        guard case let .marker(marker) = item else { return nil }
        return marker.number
    }).max() else {
        return 1
    }
    guard maxNumber < EditorDrawing.MarkerItem.maxNumber else { return nil }
    return maxNumber + 1
}
```

Placement must be updated to unwrap this optional and return without adding a marker if it is `nil`.

Inline marker editing must validate:

- Integer parse succeeds.
- Number is greater than zero.
- Number is at most `EditorDrawing.MarkerItem.maxNumber`.
- Invalid input leaves the existing number unchanged, with clean cancel behavior.

### Testing requirements

At minimum, add or update tests covering:

- Text → Marker editing cleanup.
- Marker → Text editing cleanup.
- Cursor invalidation after mutation paths, especially undo/redo/clear/delete-highest.
- Palette color updates and marker preview invalidation.
- Marker number maximum.
- `Int.max`/unexpected restored values do not overflow or crash.
- Exhausted range refuses placement.
- Existing numbered-marker behavior remains passing.
- Full test suite passes.

## 4. Additional Instructions

- Do not reproduce entire source files in reports; cite paths and line ranges instead.
- Keep code excerpts short.
- Final handoff must be one JSON object with fields:
  - `outcome`
  - `summary`
  - `findings`
  - `changes`
  - `decisions`
  - `evidence`
  - `checks`
  - `open_issues`
  - `next_steps`
- Use empty arrays where applicable.
- Report failed checks even if later corrected.
- Distinguish observed facts from assumptions.
- Do not claim PR lifecycle status unless explicitly provided by authoritative context.
- The current context indicates no PR status.

## 5. Errors and Fixes

### Initial marker test failure

The first targeted marker test run had one failing test:

- `testClickingPlacesSequentiallyNumberedMarkersInCurrentColor`
- Expected markers `[1, 2, 3]`, received `[1, 2]`.
- The third click was within the hit radius of an existing marker because test points were too close together.
- The product behavior was correct: clicking an existing marker selects/drags it instead of placing another marker.
- The test was fixed by spacing click coordinates farther apart.
- Rerun passed all 17 numbered-marker tests.

### Full suite after initial implementation

`swift test` passed:

- 246 tests executed.
- 0 failures.

### Current review fixes

No test result has yet been recorded after the most recent review-fix edits. Work was interrupted immediately after applying the first round of changes for the four review issues.

## 6. Problem Solving

### Completed before the current review

The original marker implementation solved:

- Codable marker persistence.
- Marker rendering and export.
- Marker bounds and shifting.
- State conversion.
- F shortcut and toolbar integration.
- Sequential numbering.
- Selection/movement/deletion.
- Undo/redo/clear.
- Inline marker number editing.
- Cursor preview.
- Color contrast.
- Multi-digit capsule sizing.
- PNG metadata round trip.
- Old PNG fallback behavior.
- Test coverage for 17 numbered-marker scenarios.

The implementation was compared against the baseline snapshot and only the intended marker files plus `NumberedMarkerTests.swift` and README changes differed from baseline. Pre-existing dirty work in other files was preserved.

### Current review fixes already applied

The following edits have been made:

1. Added `EditorDrawing.MarkerItem.maxNumber = 999_999`.
2. Added maximum-number validation to `EditorCanvasState` marker safety checks.
3. Added `currentColor` `didSet` invalidation.
4. Added `onMarkerCursorInvalidation` hook.
5. Changed `setTool` to determine the editing owner (`.text` vs `.marker`) and end editing only on an actual tool change.
6. Made `nextMarkerNumber` optional and overflow-safe.
7. Removed redundant explicit cursor invalidation from `setColor(_:)`.

### Remaining troubleshooting

Need inspect and complete all mutation paths so invalidation is guaranteed after:

- `undo()`
- `redo()`
- `clear()`
- marker deletion
- marker placement
- any reset/state restore path

Need ensure marker placement correctly handles `nextMarkerNumber == nil`.

Need ensure inline editing uses the same max-number check.

Need add/update regression tests and run:

- Targeted numbered marker tests.
- Full `swift test`.

## 7. Pending Tasks

- Finish integrating optional `nextMarkerNumber` into marker placement.
- Confirm `invalidateMarkerCursorPreview()` invokes the test hook.
- Audit undo/redo/clear/delete-highest paths for invalidation.
- Audit direct color assignment paths and palette shortcut behavior.
- Add regression tests for:
  - Text → Marker editing.
  - Marker → Text editing.
  - Cursor invalidation after relevant operations.
  - Direct palette color assignment/shortcut.
  - Maximum supported marker number.
  - Int.max/restored-state safety.
  - Exhausted numbering range refusing placement.
- Verify inline editing rejects values above `999_999`.
- Run targeted tests.
- Run full `swift test`.
- Report exact results in the required JSON handoff.
- Do not build/install/relaunch the app.

## 8. Current Work

Immediately before the summary request, the active work was in `Sources/EditorCanvasView.swift`, following edits in `EditorImageRenderer.swift` and `EditorCanvasState.swift`.

Most recent concrete changes:

### `Sources/EditorImageRenderer.swift`

Added:

```swift
static let maxNumber = 999_999
```

inside `EditorDrawing.MarkerItem`, with comments explaining that this bounds serialized state, inline editing, and next-number calculation.

### `Sources/EditorCanvasState.swift`

Marker safety validation now requires:

```swift
marker.number >= 1
&& marker.number <= EditorDrawing.MarkerItem.maxNumber
```

along with existing center/color/diameter safety checks.

### `Sources/EditorCanvasView.swift`

`currentColor` now has a property observer:

```swift
var currentColor: NSColor = .systemRed {
    didSet { invalidateMarkerCursorPreview() }
}
```

A test/debug callback was added:

```swift
var onMarkerCursorInvalidation: (() -> Void)?
```

`setTool(_:)` now detects the editor’s owning tool:

```swift
if textEditor != nil {
    let editingTool: EditorTool = editingMarkerIndex != nil ? .marker : .text
    if tool != editingTool {
        endTextEditingIfNeeded()
    }
}
```

`setColor(_:)` was simplified to:

```swift
func setColor(_ color: NSColor) {
    currentColor = color
}
```

The previous explicit invalidation call was removed because `currentColor.didSet` now handles all assignment paths.

`nextMarkerNumber` changed from a non-optional `Int` that did `max + 1` to an optional overflow-safe value:

```swift
private var nextMarkerNumber: Int? {
    guard let maxNumber = items.lazy.compactMap({ item -> Int? in
        guard case let .marker(marker) = item else { return nil }
        return marker.number
    }).max() else {
        return 1
    }
    guard maxNumber < EditorDrawing.MarkerItem.maxNumber else { return nil }
    return maxNumber + 1
}
```

The next continuation point should be to inspect the marker placement branch around the existing marker creation code (previously around lines 850–870, now shifted by additions), update it to handle the optional, then inspect `invalidateMarkerCursorPreview()` and all mutation methods before adding tests.
</summary>
